placements.title: System pipeline structure and behavioral requirements
placements.frame: What structural and behavioral requirements does the system's pipeline impose on submissions?
placements.why: Both segments concern the pipeline's structural behavior — what it must do with a submission lacking an explicit id — naming an architectural category the graph does not yet hold.

placements.title: Pipeline must derive identifiers from content when no explicit id is provided
placements.frame: When a submission arrives without an explicit identifier, how must the pipeline generate one from the content — and through which mechanisms — to commit the file successfully?
placements.why: src-1 states the triggering condition (submission without an explicit id field) and src-2 mandates the pipeline's response (produce a slug from memory content via LLM id-gen or deterministic slugify fallback, then commit the file). Together they name a thematic subject — the pipeline's obligation to synthesize identifiers from content when none is provided — that future envelopes about id generation, fallback mechanisms, or pipeline behavior would feed. The conviction gradient (flat claim in src-1, performed mandate in src-2) is the condition-then-obligation structure, not a thematic split.
